# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# cargo-vet ratchet baseline: the number of unvetted dependencies.
# The FIRST bare-number line of this file is the baseline
# (scripts/check-cargo-vet.sh reads it with `grep -E '^[0-9]+$' | head -1`).
#
# 437 = the first real measurement in which cargo-vet actually RAN in this
# repository (2026-07-26). Before that supply-chain/config.toml contained
# invented keys so the tool fell over with a parse error; the file's existence
# gave the impression of auditing, but not a single dependency had been audited.
#
# Rule: this number MUST NOT RISE. Lowering it is free and encouraged - when it
# drops, this file is lowered in a deliberate PR (the ratchet tightens). Raising
# the number counts as CI softening.
#
# Import coverage was measured (2026-07-26): `cargo vet regenerate imports`
# pulled 268 audit records for 158 crates from six trusted sources (Mozilla,
# Google, Bytecode Alliance, ISRG, Embark, Zcash) - imports.lock is 74 KB. Even
# so the number stays at 437: the measurement gave an identical result with
# imports.lock full and completely empty (437 = 437, zero crates closed).
# The reason is that cargo-vet requires an exact version/delta match; the
# fetched audits do not cover our locked versions. So the baseline is NOT
# inflated by "imports not fetched yet", it shows the real audit debt.
#
# Debt paydown priority (the crypto/FFI surface first):
#   ring, pqcrypto-dilithium, cryptoki, bls12_381, aes-gcm, chacha20
